origins.section: A Visibility Bug Disappears Under -Xint, C1, a Breakpoint or a Log Line: That Is the Diagnosis, Not a Fix
volatile Covers Reads of the Field, Not the Object It Points To
A volatile Array Gives Its Elements No Edge: Use AtomicIntegerArray or a VarHandle
Settings Are One Immutable Snapshot, Replaced Whole and Read Once per Unit of Work

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-halt-under-xint: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-halt-under-xint: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-halt-under-xint: The page names this exact pattern: the hang 'goes away under -Xint or with that one method excluded from compilation' points to 'a read the JIT was allowed to hoist', and C2's code 'most likely read `paused` once, before the loop: the memory model allows it because no happens-before edge leads from the write to the read'. The page hedges with 'most likely' where the key states it flatly, but the diagnosis section still decides it over the other options.
recorded.prompt:q-catalog-map-put: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-catalog-map-put: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-catalog-map-put: The page shows that `settings.setPaused(true)` 'is a volatile *read* of `settings` followed by a plain write... What publishes is a volatile *write*, and this code has none.' The reference table backs it: `holder.obj.x = 1` with `holder` volatile gives 'no: the write to `x` is plain'. Even a reader that rereads the field gets no guarantee ('the JLS allows it to return `false` forever').
recorded.prompt:q-tenant-flags-parameter: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tenant-flags-parameter: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-tenant-flags-parameter: The page's output 'volatile, as a parameter  still charging 1 s later' and its text 'Passed to a method as a parameter, the array is a plain reference, and the worker hangs as with the `final` array' decide it. The reference table agrees: `arr[i] = 1` with field `arr` volatile, read via 'a[i] on a held reference' gives 'no: the element write is plain'. The page uses boolean[], but nothing it says depends on the element type.
recorded.prompt:q-report-holds-flags: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-report-holds-flags: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-report-holds-flags: The page says 'A snapshot reaches a reader only when the reader reads the field again'. In its output the once-per-batch reader, which holds `Settings s = store.current()`, sent '4 after' the pause, and the page adds that it would be 'never, if the worker reads its settings in its constructor'. Published snapshots are immutable ('this one untouched').

recorded.prompt:q-halt-under-xint:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-halt-under-xint:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-halt-under-xint:b: The page says 'None of the switches that stopped the worker changes what the memory model allows' and that the one-time read is something 'the memory model allows', so it is not a JIT bug, and compiled code is not required to read the field on every turn the way the interpreter does.
recorded.prompt:q-halt-under-xint:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-halt-under-xint:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-halt-under-xint:c: The page says 'no cache hides the write: the hardware keeps caches coherent (unit 5.1.2)'. Each switch only 'changes which code runs', so a cache flush plays no part.
recorded.prompt:q-halt-under-xint:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-halt-under-xint:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-halt-under-xint:d: Partly true: the page says '-Xint keeps every method in the interpreter, which reads the field on every turn'. But the conclusion is refuted, because the fix is 'an edge: `volatile`, a lock both sides take, or an atomic class', and 'A passing run under any of those switches proves nothing about the production JVM'.
recorded.prompt:q-catalog-map-put:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-catalog-map-put:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-catalog-map-put:a: Partly true: the checkout threads do read the volatile field each time. But the page says of the rereading worker that 'nothing guarantees it... That is how this compiler treats a volatile read, not an edge: no write happens-before the read', so the conclusion that they are promised the price is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-catalog-map-put:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-catalog-map-put:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-catalog-map-put:b: The Design Note says a volatile write 'publishes everything written before it to a reader that reads the same field and sees the value'. The checkout threads never read `lastPricedAt`, so 'to all threads' is wrong and so is the promise.
recorded.prompt:q-catalog-map-put:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-catalog-map-put:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-catalog-map-put:d: Partly true: the conclusion (no promise) is right. The reason is refuted by 'no cache hides the write: the hardware keeps caches coherent', and by the rereading worker's 'volatile read on every turn', which shows the volatile field is read again each time rather than held in a cached copy.
recorded.prompt:q-tenant-flags-parameter:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tenant-flags-parameter:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-tenant-flags-parameter:b: Partly true: the worker is not guaranteed to stop. The reason is refuted because the page says that passed as a parameter 'the array is a plain reference', which means the reference is passed and the array is not copied. The failure comes from plain accesses, not from a copy.
recorded.prompt:q-tenant-flags-parameter:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tenant-flags-parameter:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-tenant-flags-parameter:c: The page's heading says 'A volatile Array Gives Its Elements No Edge', and the summary says 'Element writes are plain'. Its output shows the parameter version 'still charging 1 s later'.
recorded.prompt:q-tenant-flags-parameter:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tenant-flags-parameter:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-tenant-flags-parameter:d: The page says '`volatileArray[3] = true` reads that field and then writes element 3 with a plain write', so the volatile field is never written. The output shows the parameter version still charging.
recorded.prompt:q-report-holds-flags:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-report-holds-flags:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-report-holds-flags:a: Partly true: the 09:00 value is right. The reason is refuted because the once-per-charge worker was already running, held on a latch mid-batch, when the pause came, and it sent '0 after it'. So the write reaches running threads that read the field again, and when a thread started does not matter.
recorded.prompt:q-report-holds-flags:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-report-holds-flags:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-report-holds-flags:c: The page says 'Nobody can change a published `Settings`' and that `pause` returns 'a new snapshot, this one untouched'. It also says 'A worker that holds the old object still has to read the field again to get the new one'.
recorded.prompt:q-report-holds-flags:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-report-holds-flags:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-report-holds-flags:d: In `chargeOncePerBatch`, `s.allows(c)` runs through a held `s` that was read once, and that worker still sent '4 after' the pause. So calls through a held reference do not read the volatile field again.
